text:
Sam: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight 'pager coordinator' that controls allocation rhythm and eviction sweep frequency so attention kernels never see jittery KV latencies.
Anya: +1. Can you sketch the responsibilities? Is this just a timer or something that knows about kernel backpressure?
Sam: Not just a timer. Responsibilities: 1) decide alloc batch sizes based on recent token throughput, 2) run proportional eviction sweeps (adaptive to fragmentation), 3) issue prefetch/prefault hints to kernels before long sequences, 4) expose simple signals for kernel handshake (`stall`, `ready`, `prefetch_ack`).
Matt: How do you avoid worst-case stalls when fragmentation is bad? sounds like compaction will be needed and compaction is expensive.
Sam: Right. Idea is to keep compaction opportunistic and bounded. Planner maintains a live fragmentation ratio per shard. If ratio > compact_threshold then schedule a bounded compaction pass (time-sliced) AND temporarily reduce alloc_batch_tokens to avoid pressuring the kernel.
Rachel: What metrics do we need to measure to tune this?
Anya: 1) per-shard fragmentation_ratio (free_bytes / total_bytes), 2) alloc_latency P50/P99, 3) kernel KV lookup latency, 4) prefetch hit rate, 5) compaction time per MB.
Sam: Suggested defaults (can bikeshed):
```yaml
pager:
  sweep_interval_ms: 40
  alloc_batch_tokens: 8192
  compaction_threshold: 0.72
  compaction_time_slice_ms: 5
  prefault_window_tokens: 256
```
Matt: That prefault_window seems conservative. For long-context attention (8k-32k) we may want dynamic windowing. Maybe base on incoming sequence length distribution.
Sam: Agreed. Coordinator will sample recent seq_len histogram and compute expected next N tokens; prefault_window = clamp(mean_seq_len * 0.1, min=64, max=1024).
Rachel: How do kernels signal backpressure? We must avoid adding a synchronous RPC on every token.
Sam: Keep signals coarse-grained: kernel exposes a small shared-state enum per worker: `OK`, `BUSY`, `NEED_PREFETCH`, updated at boundaries (e.g., every 32 tokens or at batch start). Coordinator polls these every sweep. Kernels should react to `NEED_PREFETCH` by fetching upcoming KV pages or stubbing a fast-path.
Matt: What about eviction ordering? LRU is not great with attention patterns. We should consider frequency-adaptive lanes: hot (recent prefix), cold (long-unused), and sticky (pinned by kernel).
Anya: Exactly. Use three lanes and eviction policies per lane. When a kernel marks a page `sticky` we bump its lane and exclude it from normal sweep. Stickies have lease timeouts so we don't leak memory.
Sam: Example flow: kernel begins long seq -> posts `NEED_PREFETCH` with list of page ids -> coordinator schedules prefetch, increases alloc_batch_tokens for next sweep, and sets short compaction backoff. Once kernel responds `prefetch_ack` we let normal allocation resume.
Rachel: Any API sketch for the kernel-coordinator handshake? something tiny please.
Sam: Rough RPC/event model: 1) kernel -> coordinator: `PrefetchRequest { pages: [id,...], expected_tokens: N }` 2) coordinator -> kernel: `PrefetchScheduled { eta_ms }` (fire-and-forget) 3) coordinator signals state via shared mem: `ShardState { enum: OK|BUSY|NEED_PREFETCH, frag_ratio: float }` 4) kernel fetches pages from local cache/IO, posts `PrefetchAck`.
Matt: IO constraints: on cold pages prefetch will hit disk; need to limit concurrent disk fetches per node. Coordinator should enforce a per-node disk-fence.
Sam: Yep — add `max_concurrent_disk_fetches` and track in-flight. Coordinator queues prefetches and exposes queue length to sched.
Anya: How do we reason about tail latency? If coordinator over-aggressively compacts we might add jitter. Could we make compaction background-only unless frag_ratio > 0.9?
Sam: We already cap compaction cost via `compaction_time_slice_ms`. Background compaction runs when frag_ratio > background_compact_threshold (e.g., 0.6). Emergency compaction when > emergency_threshold (e.g., 0.9) triggers aggressive but still bounded passes and signals kernels to throttle.
Rachel: Any quick experiments to validate?
Sam: Proposal test matrix:
- Synthetic trace A: lots of short chats (2-32 tokens) -> expect low frag and small batches.
- Trace B: mixed long tails (8k tokens) -> validate prefetch hit-rate and tail latency.
- Trace C: adversarial fragmented writes (random page churn) -> validate compaction stabilizes memory and P99 alloc latency.
We should run microbench with kernel in-process and measure: tokens/sec, P50/P95/P99 alloc latency, kernel stall events, prefetch hit rate.
Matt: Also measure cost: tokens per MB moved during compaction.
Sam: One more implementation detail: KVPage leases. Use `KVPage::lease()` with a lightweight epoch token so kernels can pin without copying. Lease includes `lease_id` and `expiry_ts`. Coordinator keeps lease table and opportunistically reclaims expired leases in sweeps.
Anya: That helps with sticky pages leaking forever. Good.
infra-bot: Perf run 2043216799: synthetic-B 100 concurrent sessions -> baseline tokens/sec 18k, P99 alloc 17ms, prefetch hit 62%.
Sam: Nice — baseline looks realistic. Targets: bring P99 alloc < 10ms and prefetch hit > 85% for long-seq traces.
Rachel: Action items: Sam to draft mini-RFC with API sketches and test plan; Matt to prototype compaction time-slicing; Anya to add dashboards for frag_ratio + prefetch queue length.
Sam: I'll put the RFC in /docs/rfcs/pager-coordinator and ping this thread when done. Thanks all. :pray:
Matt: I'll stub a simulation harness for adversarial churn.
Anya: I'll wire up the metric set to the console and add alerts.
Rachel: Assign owners in RFC please.
Sam: Will do. Closing for now.
